List the datasets in the catalog

Source: R/datasets.R
gcd_datasets.Rd

The catalog of everything the API publishes, one row per dataset. With no arguments it returns every dataset: all subject areas, detail levels and years, tables and geometry alike. Each argument only narrows the list (the filtering runs on the server). About 176 datasets: small enough to View() or filter with dplyr.

The six lookup tables (districts, schools, counties, tracts, block groups, demographics) are not datasets and are not listed; see gcd_dimension().

Usage

gcd_datasets(
  main_topic = NULL,
  level = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  kind = NULL,
  details = FALSE
)

Arguments

main_topic

A single subject area: "education", "census", "health" or "immigration". Default NULL: all.

level

Keep datasets that publish rows at this detail level, such as "schools", "districts", "counties" or "tracts". Default NULL: all.

year

Keep datasets that cover this year (a single number). Default NULL: all.

kind

"table" or "geometry". Default NULL: both.

details

FALSE (default) gives the compact catalog. TRUE adds the long columns (description, source, grain and more).

Value

A tibble, one row per dataset, with columns:

  • name: the dataset's name, used by every other function.

  • title, summary: what it holds.

  • kind: "table" or "geometry".

  • main_topic: the subject area.

  • detail_levels: list-column of the levels it publishes.

  • year_min, year_max: integer, the years covered.

With details = TRUE, also: description, source, source_url, grain (list-column: the columns that identify a row), default_detail, year_gaps (list-column of missing years), update_frequency, search_aliases_en and search_aliases_es (list-columns of everyday search phrases), and updated_at (POSIXct, UTC). Geometry datasets have NA where a field doesn't apply.

See also

gcd_search() to rank datasets by plain words; gcd_describe() for one dataset.

Other find data: gcd_search()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
gcd_datasets()
gcd_datasets(main_topic = "education", level = "schools")
gcd_datasets(kind = "geometry", details = TRUE)
}
